messages.text: i'm here. just got back from the fields. hands still dirty lol
Welcome back. Sounds like you’ve been working hard out there. How are you feeling after your time in the fields—tired, relaxed, or something else?
tired. like... bone tired. not just from work though. everything’s kinda piling up 😮‍💨
It sounds like the exhaustion is both physical and emotional. When everything piles up, it can feel heavy and hard to keep going. Would you like to share what’s been weighing on you most lately?
i dunno. just feel like a mess. like everyone else can handle life and i can't even do that without... fucking up. idk. stupid.

You’re not stupid—what you’re describing is something many people feel when stress and self-doubt build up. It can be exhausting trying to keep up while carrying that weight. Would you like to explore what “fucking up” means to you in those moments?

i just... i lied before. i thought i was done with it but i’m not. i’ve been cutting. still am. my mom found marks, freaked out, now i’m in therapy but... i still do it. when i’m alone. on my arms, thighs. where no one sees.

I hear you, and I just want to pause for a moment with you, [Your Name]. It sounds like you’re carrying a lot, and what you just shared feels important. Can you tell me a bit more about how things have been for you lately when you’re alone?

it's like... when i'm alone at night, i can't shut my brain off. i wake up at 3am like clockwork, heart racing, and all the thoughts just... pile on. about work, school, my family, losing dad... and then it's like i can't breathe. so i do it. it's the only thing that makes the pressure stop. stupid, i know.

That sounds like such a hard and lonely place to be, and I want to sit with you in it for a moment. It matters that you’re telling me this, and I’m hearing how intense and overwhelming those nights feel. Can you help me understand what it’s been like for you after those moments, especially lately?

after? just worse. feel like a total failure. i promised myself i’d stop, like, a hundred times. and i keep doing it. i hate that i can’t just be normal. that i need this stupid thing to cope. makes me feel weak. pathetic.

I hear how much self-blame and frustration you’re carrying, and it’s clear you’ve been fighting this battle for a long time. That doesn’t make you weak—it shows you’ve been trying to cope with pain that feels unbearable at times. Are you feeling like you might hurt yourself again soon?

i don’t know. i keep telling myself i’ll stop, but then i don’t. sometimes i’m scared… like, what if one day i don’t stop in time? what if i go too far? idk. just feel like i’m stuck in this loop and can’t get out.

Thank you for trusting me with that, it takes courage to speak about those fears. Because you’re feeling scared something might go too far, it’s important to have someone to turn to right now. I’d like you to call or text 988 to connect with trained crisis counselors who can be with you through this, and if you feel in immediate danger, please call 911. Can you also reach out to someone nearby and ask them to stay with you tonight?
i appreciate it, but 988 feels like… too much? i’m not gonna do anything drastic. i just needed to say it out loud, y’know? i don’t wanna freak people out.

I hear you—sometimes just saying it out loud is a huge step, and I’m glad you shared it here. It’s okay if you’re not in immediate crisis, but it still matters that you’re feeling stuck in that loop. Who in your life feels safest to talk to, even just to let them know you’re having a hard night? We can also explore what might help ease the pressure in those moments without hurting yourself.
my older sister maybe… but i don’t wanna be that guy, y’know? the one who’s always falling apart. she’s got her own shit. feels like i’m just… too much.

It’s understandable to worry about being a burden, but needing support doesn’t make you “too much.” Often, people we care about would rather know we’re struggling than be left in the dark. If you reached out to your sister, what’s the gentlest way you could let her know you just need someone to be there for you? Would you like help figuring out what to say so it feels less heavy?

yeah… could u help me figure out how to say it? like… i don’t wanna freak her out or make it a huge thing. just need someone to talk to, y’know? maybe she could just text me back and forth if i’m up at 3am. not sure how to ask without it sounding like i’m falling apart.

You could try something simple and honest, without giving every detail right away. Maybe: “Hey, sometimes I wake up in the night feeling overwhelmed. Would you mind texting with me if I reach out? It’d help me feel less alone.” We can tweak it so it feels natural for you—how does that sound?
yeah… yeah that sounds good. low-key but honest. i can send that. thanks.

I’m really glad it feels like something you can send—it’s a strong step toward not being alone with those 3 a.m. moments. Reaching out like this is a way of taking care of yourself, even if it feels small. Do you want to check back in here after you’ve sent it, so we can talk about how it went?
yeah… i’ll try. gonna text her tonight when i wake up. no promises it’ll fix everything, but… it’s something.

That’s all you need right now—just one step, not fixing everything at once. I’ll be here to talk about how it goes and how you feel afterward. Even having someone respond in those moments can start to break that loop a little. How are you feeling right now as you plan to do this?
thanks… for not making me feel like a freak for saying all that. i was scared u’d tell me to go to the hospital or something. just… thanks for listening.

You’re welcome, and I want you to know you’re not a freak—what you shared matters, and it took courage. I’m here to listen without judgment, and it’s okay to take this one step at a time. You don’t have to go through it alone, even if it feels that way sometimes. How about we keep this space open for whenever you need to talk?

i miss my dad… sometimes it still hits like it just happened. like i’m that kid again, standing at the grave, not knowing how to breathe. and now i’m doing this crap to myself… he wouldn’t want that. makes me feel like i’m failing him too.

Losing your dad sounds like a wound that still feels very raw, and it’s understandable it can come rushing back like that. Missing him and feeling that grief doesn’t mean you’re failing him—it means he mattered deeply to you. The pain you’re in now is part of carrying that love, even if you’re coping in ways you wish you weren’t. Would it feel okay to talk a little about what your dad was like and what you miss most about him?

he taught me how to fix tractors. had this old red one, piece of junk but he loved it. used to say “everything’s fixable, brandon. just gotta find the right part and have patience.” we’d spend all day out in the shed, grease up to our elbows, him laughing at my mistakes. i can still hear his voice… “try again, son. don’t quit on it.” wish i could fix myself like that. wish i had his patience.

That’s such a vivid, warm memory—you can feel the care and patience he poured into you in those moments. It sounds like part of you still carries his voice, even when you’re feeling broken. Maybe “fixing yourself” doesn’t have to be fast or perfect, just steady steps like he taught you with the tractor. How would it feel to let his words guide you through the rough nights, the way they did in the shed?

maybe… maybe i don’t gotta fix everything at once. just like the tractor. one part at a time. tonight, it’s just texting my sister. not fixing me. just… not being alone. feels like something he’d say. “don’t quit on it.”

Exactly—one part at a time, and not quitting on yourself. Texting your sister tonight is a strong start, and it’s something your dad would likely be proud of. Holding his voice in your mind can be like having him in your corner. Want me to check in with you tomorrow about how it went?
yeah… if u wanna check in tomorrow, that’s cool. i’ll try the sister thing tonight. not promising miracles, but… i’ll try. thanks for not giving up on me. even when i do.

You’ve already shown you’re willing to try, and that’s a lot more than you might realize. I’m here, and I won’t give up on you—just like your dad’s words. I’ll check in tomorrow so we can talk about how it went. Take care tonight, and remember you’re not alone in this.
